byline: One line, for you, not the players.

job.pay: Too much, and here's why that's strange

wrongDetail: Exactly one thing is wrong and nobody comments on it. Never explain it.

locations.sense: what it smells and sounds like

clues.text: A hole in the world. Concrete, strange, explains nothing.
Something only the GM knows is on the board.

artifacts.body: A document, a log, a transcript. Let it be dull and specific.

puzzles.body: Give them a way to work the code out in the fiction.
puzzles.payload: What they get when it opens.

puzzles.body: Wrap missing words in double brackets: the log shows [[eleven]] minutes gone, every [[night]].

terrors: Ring 1 — something small and physically wrong
Ring 3 — someone lies to them specifically
Ring 4 — a rule of the world visibly breaks
temptations: Ring 1 — easy money to look the other way
Ring 2 — an answer, for a favour
Ring 3 — something they want and shouldn't take
Ring 4 — it offers to simply tell them
Ring 5 — a way out that costs somebody else

notes:
DO NOT WRITE A SOLUTION. If you have one in your head, throw it out — you'll steer toward it.

Run Ring 1 slow. Let them be good at their jobs before anything is wrong.

Depth 3. Let them find six or seven clues. Let them Theorize in Ring 4.
